node.label: Thomas J. Sugrue
node.date_label: The Origins of the Urban Crisis (1996) · The New Suburban History (co-edited with Kevin M. Kruse) (2006) · Sweet Land of Liberty (2008)
node.description: An urban historian who locates postwar racial inequality in the interaction of deindustrialization, housing and employment discrimination, and political choices. His Detroit interpretation challenges accounts that place the origins of urban poverty in the social programmes of the 1960s.

proposed_edges.relationship: Places Detroit’s urban crisis in changes already under way during the 1940s and 1950s.
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Own 1999 answers reject making 1960s social programmes the originating cause and identify industrial restructuring and housing practices.

proposed_edges.relationship: Connects racial inequality to discrimination in jobs and housing alongside the reorganization of industrial work.
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Own transcript distinguishes racialized consequences of capital flight from an explanation based on economic change alone.
